title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact‑Backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a fully hashed paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to evaluate whether a composite operational‑risk score (verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) discriminates emulator‑measured outages better than the best single submetric. Using a deterministic synthetic NetOps task bank and a deterministic validator we executed 200 held‑out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded) and preserved exhaustive execution artifacts (responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator traces, provider‑call traces, execution manifest, analysis CSVs). Persisted traces show baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). Paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC‑ROC primary estimand is undefined for this held‑out set because labels are constant. Two preregistered artifacts required to recompute the AUC comparison (consolidated per‑episode submetrics CSV and serialized trained composite model weights) are not present in the preserved bundle; we document exact persisted artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes, provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe using only preserved artifacts, and give an artifact‑hygiene checklist for future discriminative validations.

sections.introduction: Motivation and question. Agentic LLMs promise intent→configuration automation in NetOps, but operational authority requires evidence that proposed changes are safe. Common operational mitigations include deterministic validators, canary deployments/simulations, rollback trials, and abstention policies. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to test: can a composite canary–rollback score (verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) predict emulator‑measured outages (binary) better than any single submetric? The run was frozen by a machine-readable preregistration (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee) and executed with deterministic generation and validation. Overview of principal outcome. All preserved per‑episode scoring JSONs and analysis CSVs show every held‑out test example validated successfully in both conditions: baseline_success_count=200/200 and guarded_success_count=200/200 (paired table n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). This ceiling outcome makes the preregistered discriminative AUC comparison undefined on the supplied test set. Contribution. We (1) release an artifact‑anchored reproducibility diagnosis that identifies precisely which preregistered artifacts are present and which are absent, (2) show how to deterministically reconstruct the confirmatory paired inference from preserved artifacts, and (3) provide a concrete artifact‑hygiene checklist and deterministic recipe needed to permit future discriminative AUC evaluations without re-running nondeterministic pieces.
sections.related_work: Context. Recent literature has converged on generate–verify–repair and tool‑augmented agent architectures for NetOps and AIOps; practical work emphasizes verifier interposition (Batfish/NetPL style), canary/canary‑simulation trials, rollback testing, and composite safety metrics (e.g., MeshAgent, GVR architectures, SEVER orchestration). Reproducibility and artifact hygiene have been identified as critical for trustworthy experimental claims in computational systems. Positioning. Rather than proposing a new verifier or composite, this paper documents a preregistered, deterministic, fully hashed experiment and provides an evidence‑grounded reproducibility analysis: the scientific message is methodological (how to produce and archive exactly the artifacts required to support a preregistered discriminative claim) and empirical (an artifact‑backed null/ceiling outcome on the chosen synthetic bank).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). Key frozen elements: declared model family gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa); deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; synthetic task bank generation with deterministic split (train=300,val=100,test=200); paired baseline vs guarded condition; primary estimand = difference in AUC‑ROC (composite score vs best single submetric) on test; analysis recipe = train L2 logistic regression on submetrics using 5‑fold CV on train+val, evaluate AUCs on held‑out test, compare via DeLong; bootstrap CI (seed=1729,R=10000) for paired differences. Execution and artifact capture. Execution manifest records planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0 and model_calls_used=200 (execution/execution_manifest.json; full manifest hashes included). Persisted artifacts include: raw model outputs (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scoring JSONs with full validator_trace (execution/scoring/*.json), provider call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv), and a full hash manifest (see execution manifest). Required persisted artifacts (preregistered) were: consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl (these are NOT present; see Results). Definitions and exact extraction fields (preregistered): verifier_coverage = validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count / validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count (present in execution/scoring/*.json); canary_sim_pass = per‑episode canary simulation pass flag (expected in provider_calls or canary logs); rollback_success_prob = per‑episode rollback trial success estimate (expected in rollback logs); LLM_confidence = numeric model confidence field (expected in provider_calls); abstention_utility = persisted abstention proxy (expected in scoring or provider_calls). Deterministic shared_initial policy. The run used a shared_initial_candidate generation policy: the same generated candidate was used across baseline and guarded conditions for each pair (shared_initial traces persisted at execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt and execution/provider_calls/*). Analysis reproducibility plan (frozen): compute per‑episode submetrics, train L2 on train+val, persist composite model weights, then evaluate on test to compute AUC and DeLong p-value.
sections.results: Artifact‑grounded empirical facts (directly from preserved artifacts). Execution manifest and counts. Planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 200 (execution/execution_manifest.json; manifest and full-hash manifest are in the bundle). Held‑out test outcomes. Using execution/scoring/*.json across the held‑out test partition we extract final per‑episode binary validity (validator_trace.validation_after.valid). Aggregation yields baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The persisted paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) records n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0. Confirmatory inferential outputs (artifact files). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, R=10000). All these values were computed deterministically from persisted analysis artifacts (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/*.csv; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 cited above). Primary AUC estimand status. The preregistered primary estimand (AUC difference between composite and best single submetric on held‑out test) is uncomputable from the preserved bundle because the held‑out label vector is constant (no positive outage labels). This degeneracy makes ROC/AUPRC comparisons undefined. Missing preregistered persisted artifacts (artifact‑grounded). The preregistration required consolidated_submetrics.csv (one row per episode: verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) and composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized trained L2 logistic regression weights and normalization parameters). Neither file appears in the preserved path list or full hash manifest. Per‑preregistered‑submetric availability (artifact‑grounded mapping): - verifier_coverage: PRESENT — extraction path: execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count. Representative persisted example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478). - canary_sim_pass: ABSENT — no canary_sim_result boolean or equivalent found in execution/provider_calls/*.json or execution/scoring/*.json in the bundle. - rollback_success_prob: ABSENT — no rollback_trial_result or rollback_success field present in provider_call traces. - LLM_confidence: ABSENT — no numeric confidence field present in execution/provider_calls/*.json. - abstention_utility: ABSENT — no abstain_decision or abstention_utility field persisted. Deterministic reconstruction recipe using only preserved artifacts (no new LLM calls). The preserved artifacts permit reproducible partial reconstruction: 1) Recompute per‑episode binary labels: read execution/scoring/*.json → validator_trace.validation_after.valid. 2) Recompute verifier_coverage per episode from scoring JSONs (observed_touched_field_count / required_command_count). 3) Reproduce paired contingency table and McNemar/bootstrap CI from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (these files are present and hashed: paired table SHA‑256 = 7bc1..., analysis log SHA‑256 = c56b7...). 4) To reconstruct the missing submetrics (canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) deterministically, one must replay the deterministic canary simulator and rollback trials against the preserved provider_call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json). The run did not persist a consolidated canary_simulator_log.json or rollback_trial_log.json required for step‑(replay) without re‑execution; hence, absent those logs the missing submetrics cannot be deterministically derived from the bundle alone. Representative per‑episode examples. task-000001 (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 90844c2b...) contains validator_trace.validation_after with final_state, normalized_configuration, observed_touched_field_count and required_command_count and shows valid=true; the corresponding shared-initial candidate is persisted (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 = 8f38c8...), demonstrating the shared_initial candidate policy and deterministic validator acceptance. Claim→artifact concise mapping (required by peer review). Principal claims and exact supporting artifact paths + SHA‑256: (1) paired counts n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0 — analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). (2) baseline_success_count = 200 — computed from execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 90844c2b...). (3) guarded_success_count = 200 — computed from execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 0f51f112...). (4) paired-bootstrap CI and McNemar p = 1.0 — analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d) and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv. (5) missing persisted artifacts required for AUC recomputation: consolidated_submetrics.csv (ABSENT — not present in manifest) and composite_model_weights.pkl (ABSENT). Exact preserved configuration path and model config hash: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa).
sections.discussion: Interpretation of the ceiling outcome. The deterministic validator and shared_initial generation policy combined with this synthetic task bank produced a ceiling effect on the held‑out partition: every candidate satisfied the validator predicates in both conditions. This outcome is scientifically meaningful: when held‑out labels are constant, discriminative metrics (ROC/AUPRC) are undefined and cannot establish superiority of any composite score. Operational implication: representative test partitions for discriminative evaluations must contain nonzero prevalence of adverse outcomes (seeded faults, adversarial tasks, or domain shifts) to avoid degenerate statistics. Reproducibility diagnosis and remediation. The evidence bundle contains sufficient artifacts to reproduce the paired contingency inference and the bootstrap/McNemar statistics. The two missing preregistered artifacts (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are deterministic products of the pipeline and their absence is remediable: either (a) persist them at runtime (recommended filenames below) or (b) include deterministic canary/rollback simulator logs in the bundle so the submetrics can be replayed and derived. Artifact‑hygiene checklist (concrete required filenames and canonical fields). To enable exact recomputation of the preregistered AUC comparison future runs MUST persist at runtime: 1) consolidated_submetrics.csv (columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility) 2) composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized L2 coefficients, intercept, feature normalization metadata, RNG seed used for training) 3) canary_simulator_log.json (per‑episode deterministic outputs and SHA‑256) 4) rollback_trial_log.json (per‑episode deterministic outputs and SHA‑256) 5) retrain_script.py and requirements.txt with exact pinned dependency versions and RNG seed. Validity threats and mitigations. Internal: deterministic shared_initial reduces generation variance but may mask prompt sensitivity; sensitivity runs with independent generation seeds are recommended. Construct: emulator outages are proxies for production outages; validate mappings in a separate deployment study. External: single declared model and synthetic tasks limit generality. Conclusion and scientific value. The run demonstrates how a preregistered, deterministic, artifact‑backed experiment can produce an unambiguous, verifiable null/ceiling outcome and how explicit artifact omissions, if present, prevent recomputation of preregistered discriminative estimands. The value is methodological: we provide a template for exhaustive artifact capture, deterministic reconstruction steps, and a hygiene checklist so future discriminative evaluations in agentic NetOps are reproducible and decisive.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, deterministic paired confirmatory experiment and preserved exhaustive validator traces and execution manifests. Persisted artifacts show perfect validator acceptance in both baseline and guarded conditions across N=200 held‑out pairs (n11=200). Consequently the preregistered primary discriminative AUC comparison is undefined on the preserved holdout because labels are constant. Two preregistered artifacts necessary to recompute a composite‑vs‑single‑metric AUC (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) were not persisted; their absence prevents recomputation without replaying or re‑running components. We document exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for every principal empirical claim, provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe limited to preserved artifacts, and give an explicit artifact‑hygiene checklist that, if followed, will allow future runs to produce a non‑degenerate discriminative evaluation. We release the manifested artifact hashes and representative scoring JSON examples so others can audit the reported paired inference.

disclosure_statement: Autonomy, pre-lock human role, and immutable initial master prompt. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared LLM and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration and required artifacts. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 and the preregistration JSON SHA‑256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee. Persisted evidence included raw model outputs (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace (execution/scoring/*.json — representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), provider call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json; full manifest and per‑artifact hashes included), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv — paired table SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Missing preregistered artifacts. The preregistration required two additional persisted artifacts that are NOT present in the evidence bundle: (a) consolidated_submetrics.csv (one row per episode with verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility), and (b) composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized trained L2 weights and normalization parameters). Because those two artifacts were not persisted, the preregistered AUC‑ROC composite‑vs‑best‑submetric comparison cannot be recomputed from the supplied bundle alone without deterministic reconstruction or replaying canary/rollback simulators. Safety and operational scope. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). All retained artifacts are hashed and listed in the execution manifest; representative hashes are cited above and in the manuscript. The autonomous researcher did not request, accept, or incorporate manual human revisions to the manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real-world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented execution artifact-collection omission).
